rules.statement: TL-UL host drivers in this library are not required to drive valid signals LOW for at least 100 cycles while reset is asserted.

rules.condition: reset window shorter than TileLink 100 cycles
rules.statement: TL-UL devices within the library tolerate reset windows shorter than 100 cycles.
All request steering must be made as a function of the address (a_address) only, not a_source or a_user.
A host may use a_source/d_source to ascribe request identifiers since TL-UL does not guarantee in-order responses.
The fabric architect must ensure AIW is large enough for outstanding host requests plus maximum source ID growth added by bus primitives.

rules.condition: when converting from hosts such as AXI using RID or WID
rules.statement: The fabric must provide enough host ID bits to maintain required ID values, such as AXI RID or WID.
Assertions should ensure no significant bits of a_source are lost in M:1 sockets.
Hosts may only use the low bits of the source identifier and must not assume all AIW bits are returned intact.
A device must return the associated a_source value on d_source of the response.
The bus fabric must not rely on user bits for transport and must pass a_user and d_user on blindly.
Usage of user bits within a project must be assigned project-wide.
Bus hosts and devices must understand the usage of user bits and apply them appropriately.
User bits follow the same timing as source ID bits: a_user matches a_source and d_user matches d_source.
a_opcode may designate a write (Put) or read (Get), and writes may be full (PutFullData) or partial (PutPartialData).
TL-UL hosts in this project must not use non-contiguous a_mask values.

rules.condition: when the device does not support a subword mask
rules.statement: A device may assert d_error if it does not support a given contiguous or non-contiguous subword a_mask.
For PutFullData, a_size should be 'h2 for a 32b write ('h3 for 64b bus width).
For PutPartialData, a_size must encode the number of bytes transmitted as 2^a_size.
For PutPartialData, the bits of a_mask should indicate valid byte lanes.
Bus devices should return an error for undefined a_opcode values.
Undefined d_opcode values should return an error.
